note: Private campground at I-57 exit 40, a few miles from Lake of Egypt and the Shawnee National Forest; highway noise carries. Back-in rows sit in shade, pull-throughs in the open; LP fill, playground, pavilion, overflow parking for boats. Monthly sites are rented alongside nightly ones, so part of the park holds long-term campers. --Claude
summary: Operator site, map, rules and the ResNexus engine read: 35 full-hookup sites (15 pull-through), $45 nightly (also $280 weekly, $685 monthly), open all year, showers, laundry, wifi; online booking on ResNexus. Google 4.6/184. Passes the $50 gate; no gateway; Good Sam not stored. Markets monthly/seasonal stays alongside nightly ones: keep with a long-term caveat. Not waterfront kept.
flags: GATE FACTS (private): $45/night posted on the operator's homepage and quoted by ResNexus for 2026-11-12 (under $50, passes). Good Sam: not in the Good Sam directory (local cache trip_data/goodsam_parks.json, fetched 2026-10-02), so not a GS Park. Gateway: none within 40 km (gateways.py). Presence: live site, online booking, Google open, 4.6 stars from 184 reviews.

LONG-STAY five tests: (1) monthly and seasonal stays ARE marketed ('affordable monthly camping', 'a seasonal stay, or long-term RV camping', '$685 monthly', 'Please call us ... regarding monthly rentals'); (2) a nightly rate is posted and bookable online 24 hours; (3) no lots or homes for sale; (4) imagery shows ~15 RVs, many tucked under canopy in the back-in rows, typical of longer stays; ResNexus showed 12 results (cabin + about 11 sites) open for a 2-night stay starting Thu 2026-11-12, i.e. at least ~a third of the 35 sites are sold by the night; (5) no wording discouraging nightly guests ('reserve online 24 hours a day', night check-in). Nightly share measured at roughly a third or more (10-50% band) -> keep with the long-term-campers caveat now in the note. Reviewer may weigh the 'road noise' review topic (13 mentions).
OHV: the rules allow 'privately owned golf carts and ATV's on our properties' (on the grounds only); no trail access is marketed, so not an OHV base.
